Albany by the numbers

Who sends and collects the property tax bill in Albany, NY?

The City of Albany Treasurer collects the bill, and the City Assessor sets the value it is based on. The Treasurer's office is in City Hall at 24 Eagle Street, and the phone number is 518-434-5036. The Assessor's office is on the third floor of the same building in Room 302, reachable at 518-434-5155.

Albany sits on the west bank of the Hudson River, about ten miles south of where the Mohawk River joins it, and has been New York's capital since 1797. The city is also the seat of Albany County, and its housing ranges from row houses near the river to newer streets around Buckingham Pond. Under the City Charter the Treasurer is the chief fiscal officer and handles collection of all city taxes and money owed to the city.

  • Treasurer: tax bills, payments, receipts, address changes, returned payments.
  • Assessor: assessed values, STAR and other exemption applications, grievance forms, parcel maps.
  • Board of Assessment Review: hears assessment complaints. The Common Council appoints its members to five-year terms.

When are Albany property taxes due, and what happens if I pay late?

The full bill, or the first half if you split it, is due by January 31. Eligible seniors get until February 6. When January 31 lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day, and in 2027 that falls on a Sunday, so the practical date is Monday, February 1.

Albany now lets every owner pay in two installments. The first installment is half the bill. The second half is billed in early July and can be paid any time after the first installment, with interest added. Installments must be paid by check or cash, because the online system takes full payments only.

Bills should reach your mailbox by January 12. If yours has not come by then, print it from the Treasurer's online lookup instead of calling. The city states that state law requires penalties on late payments in every case, and the municipality cannot waive the interest. A returned payment costs $34.

What is the waste collection fee on an Albany tax bill?

It is a separate charge of $180 per unit that appears on the property tax bill itself. Before 2026 the city mailed that fee as its own bill. Unpaid amounts from the prior year, listed as $90 per unit for 2025, are carried onto the 2026 tax bill along with added late charges.

Owners who believe the fee should not apply to them can email the Treasurer or call 518-434-5036 to request an exemption application. The city notes that it did not place the fee on 2025 bills for owners it already knew to be exempt in 2023 and 2024.

This matters when you sell. A previous year's fee that went unpaid becomes part of the tax bill, so it belongs in the payoff total. Ask the Treasurer for a figure that includes it, and check the total against the bill you received in January.

How do I pay my Albany property tax?

You can pay by mail, online, or in person at City Hall. The office recommends against bill-payment services, because their envelopes usually carry no postmark, and the city counts the date by the USPS postmark and ignores a postage meter mark.

  • By mail: make the check payable to City of Albany and send it to City Treasurer, Room 109, City Hall, Albany, NY 12207. Include the bill number, your signature and the date, plus any interest owed.
  • Online: e-check costs 50 cents. A credit card costs 25 cents plus 1.95 percent of the payment. Online payments can take up to five business days to show.
  • In person: Room 110 at City Hall, weekdays from 8:30 a.m., with later hours from January 29 to 31.

Send a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want a receipt right away. Otherwise receipts go out in bulk in late March or April, and e-receipts post online within 48 hours of a payment.

How do I challenge an Albany assessment?

File a grievance complaint with the Assessor after May 1 and no later than Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. Forms are available at the Assessor's office starting May 1. The Board of Assessment Review decides the complaint under Chapter 42 of the Albany General Code.

Assessments change in Albany because of new construction, fires, demolitions and periodic citywide updates meant to keep the roll even. You can look at any parcel on the maps kept in the Assessor's office. Bring a recent sale of a similar house nearby, a repair estimate or an appraisal, since the board decides on value and does not weigh how large the bill feels.

Which exemptions and STAR benefits apply in Albany?

Exemption applications are accepted from January 1 through March 1, filed at the Assessor's office. Basic STAR is for owners who live in the home, and every owner must sign the application and supply a photocopy of a driver's license as proof of residence. Call 518-434-5155 for help with Enhanced STAR.

The state's Tax Department now pays STAR as a credit you register for once. It issues the payment before your school tax is due and keeps paying each year while you stay eligible. Anyone who sells the home should close the registration, and the buyer registers as soon as the house is a primary residence.

What happens to unpaid Albany tax when I sell the house?

Any balance is settled from your sale proceeds at closing, and the current year is split between you and the buyer on the closing statement. You do not need to bring cash to the table, but the payoff has to be right, so ask the Treasurer for the number before the closing date. The office takes calls at 518-434-5036 on weekdays.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance, including any carried-over waste collection fee, and keep the answer in an email.
  • If the first installment is paid and the July half is not yet billed, expect a proration credit to the buyer for the months you owned.
  • Confirm with the Assessor that your exemption is removed or transferred in line with the new owner's status.

A buyer who pays cash and closes quickly can settle the same payoff, so owing the city does not stop a sale. It only changes how much is left for you after the closing statement.

What does the housing market around Albany look like?

Albany is a small, dense city of about 21 square miles. Older sections near the river are mostly row houses, which often carry older roofs, porches and boilers that a buyer will inspect. The Pine Bush preserve, once about 25,000 acres, has shrunk to roughly 6,000 acres because of development on the city's western edge.

With owners in fewer than four of ten homes, many Albany sellers are landlords of small multifamily buildings. They should confirm each unit's waste collection fee before the payoff request.

More questions about Albany, NY Property Tax Guide

What is the Albany property tax deadline?

January 31, or February 6 for eligible seniors, with the next business day used when it falls on a weekend. In 2027 that moves the deadline to February 1. Mailed payments count by USPS postmark.

Can I split my Albany tax bill into two payments?

Yes. Pay half by the January deadline and the rest after the July bill goes out, with interest. The installment option accepts checks or cash only and is unavailable online.

Where do I get a copy of my Albany tax bill or receipt?

From the Treasurer's online lookup or by emailing the Treasurer's billing address. Receipts are mailed in bulk in late March or April, and online receipts appear within 48 hours.

When is Albany Grievance Day?

It is the fourth Tuesday in May. Forms are available from May 1 at the Assessor's office in City Hall Room 302, and the complaint must be filed by Grievance Day.

Do I owe Albany tax if I sell mid-year?

You owe the share for the months you owned the house. The closing statement splits the year, and any unpaid balance is paid to the Treasurer from your proceeds, so request the payoff figure before the closing date.

Who bills and collects property tax in Amherst, NY?

The Amherst Town Clerk's office doubles as the Receiver of Taxes and collects the Town and County bill, while the Assessor's Office sets the assessed value. Both work out of Town Hall at 5583 Main Street in Williamsville. The Town Clerk's number is 716-631-7021, and the Assessor's is 716-631-7038.

Amherst is a suburb of Buffalo in northern Erie County. The state created it in 1818 out of the town of Buffalo, and it covers 53.6 square miles that include the village of Williamsville and the hamlets of Eggertsville, Getzville, Snyder, Swormville and East Amherst. A property tax bill here has several layers, so know which office answers which question.

  • Town Clerk and Receiver of Taxes: Town and County tax bills and payments.
  • Assessor: values, exemptions, name and mailing address corrections, assessment challenges.
  • Village of Williamsville Clerk: village tax for properties inside the village, at 632-4120 (option 9).
  • Your school district: school tax dates are set separately, so ask the district.

When is Amherst Town and County tax due?

The due date is February 15. When that day lands on a weekend, the town extends it, and for 2026 the deadline was Tuesday, February 17, because February 15 was a Sunday and Town Hall was closed on the Monday holiday. The town's notice also says full and partial payments are accepted at the Town Clerk's office until June 30, with penalties added after the deadline.

The Town Clerk's office is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and does not close for lunch. A drop box at the back door of Town Hall is available around the clock, and a payment left there after hours and before midnight on the due date is not treated as late.

Property tax is not lump sum only. The assessor's FAQ says partial payments are accepted in any dollar amount, as many times as needed, but any balance left after the due date accrues interest and penalties on the schedule printed on the back of the bill.

How can I make sure my Amherst payment is not late?

Deliver it in a way that does not rely on a mailbox postmark. In December 2025 the postal service explained that a postmark now reflects the day mail reaches a regional processing hub, which can add one to three days after you drop it at a local post office.

  • Ask for a hand-stamped postmark at a post office counter.
  • Send it by certified or registered mail.
  • Use the Town Hall drop box at the back entrance.
  • Pay online through the town website, where you search your owner name or address in the tax bill lookup.
  • Pay in person at the Town Clerk's office.

The town discourages paying through your bank's online bill pay. Those checks arrive in bulk mail from a processing center with no postmark at all, and the town says anyone who uses that route does so at their own risk.

How do I challenge my Amherst assessment?

Start with an informal review at the Assessor's Office, then file a formal complaint on form RP-524 before Grievance Day. The next Grievance Day is Tuesday, May 25, 2027, and the town says to check back after May 1 for the hearing details.

Informal review information is posted each year after March 1. The 2026 roll used a valuation date of July 1, 2025 and a taxable status date of March 1, 2026. The Assessor offers separate review applications for residential, condominium, commercial and vacant land parcels.

The town stresses that the Assessor does not set the tax levy. Your case should rest on market value, supported by comparable sales of similar houses in your area, with attention to location, style, age and size. A five-year-old house and a fifty-year-old house are not comparable. Copies you hand in stay with the Board of Assessment Review, so keep your own set.

What does Amherst's official page say about buying or selling mid-year?

The owner on the tax due date answers for the whole bill, whether or not the bill arrived. If you bought partway through the year, you still owe the entire bill, though the closing statement normally prorates it and the seller credits you for the months before you owned the house.

The page explains that the attorney who handled the closing calculates that credit, and the seller does not send any partial payment to the tax collector. For a seller, this means the unpaid current tax should be settled from your proceeds by the closing attorney, and the number on the closing statement should match the Receiver's own figure.

If the name or mailing address on the bill is wrong, the Assessor, not the Town Clerk, corrects it. Fix that before listing so the bill does not go astray during the sale. The Assessor also answers questions about the RPTL charge on a Town and County bill, a line that can represent one-time charges rather than regular tax, so ask about it before you assume the payoff is wrong.

What does it cost to own a house in the Town of Amherst?

The numbers below describe the whole town, which includes Williamsville and the hamlets. A given street can run well above or below them. The town is also home to the north campus of the University at Buffalo and to a campus of Erie Community College, which is worth knowing if your house sits near either.

What should I check before selling an Amherst house with tax due?

Ask for the exact balance before the closing, because partial payments, penalties and any village charges can all change it. A short checklist keeps the sale on schedule.

  • If the property is in Williamsville, call the village clerk for the village portion.
  • Ask your school district for its balance, since it bills on its own schedule.
  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on file with the Assessor.

A buyer paying cash can close on a short timeline, and the payoffs come out of the sale price just as in a financed sale.

What is the Amherst property tax due date?

February 15 for Town and County tax. In 2026 it moved to Tuesday, February 17 because the 15th fell on a Sunday and Town Hall was closed Monday. Partial payments are accepted at the Town Clerk's office until June 30.

Can I pay Amherst taxes in installments?

Yes, in any dollar amount and as many payments as it takes. Any unpaid balance after the due date accrues interest and penalties, as shown on the schedule on the back of your bill.

Is there a drop box for Amherst tax payments?

Yes. It sits at the back door of Town Hall at 5583 Main Street and is open around the clock. Payments left there after hours, up to midnight on the due date, are not counted as late.

Who collects property tax in the Town of Brookhaven, NY?

The Town's Receiver of Taxes collects the bill from December 1 through May 31, and the Suffolk County Comptroller takes over after that. The tax office sits in Town Hall at 1 Independence Hill in Farmingville, and its phone number is 631-451-9009. The Assessor works from the same building.

Brookhaven is the second most populous town in New York, a Suffolk County town on Long Island with a 2020 Census count of 485,773 and 259.65 square miles of land. Its first English settlement, at Setauket, dates to 1655. The town reaches from Port Jefferson and Stony Brook on the North Shore to Patchogue on the South Shore, so a single tax office serves hamlets with very different school districts and home prices.

The Receiver's office says it only collects. It does not set rates. School budgets come from your school district, the county levy from the county budget, and the town levy from the Supervisor and Town Board.

What is the Brookhaven tax year, and when are bills mailed?

Town, county and school taxes in Suffolk County cover December 1 through November 30 of the following year. The bill becomes a lien on December 1, and the town mails it in mid-December. The town says you should have it by December 15. If it has not come by the third week of December, call the tax office.

The online tax system closed for the 2025 to 2026 tax year on June 1, 2026, and stays offline until the new season opens in December 2026. That puts the next bill a few weeks away from today. Owners with a mortgage escrow account get an informational bill around mid-July instead, while the lender receives the payment copy directly.

What are the Brookhaven due dates and late charges?

The first half is due January 10 and the second half May 31. The town accepts one bill split into two payments. After the first-half date, the interest steps up each month, and the final day to pay without going delinquent is May 31.

Taxpayers who receive Enhanced STAR or the over-65 exemption get five more business days after May 31. Beyond that date, the account is delinquent and payable to the Suffolk County Comptroller, who adds a 5 percent penalty and interest of 1 percent per month counted from February 1. The town is not part of the delinquency process.

How do I pay my Brookhaven taxes?

Pay online, in person, or by mail, but watch the postmark rules. A federal change that took effect December 24, 2025 means mail dropped in a box may not get a same-day postmark. The town says the only guaranteed method is a hand-stamped envelope at a post office counter, and the tax office cannot waive penalties when a payment lacks a timely postmark.

  • Online: an e-check costs $1.75, and a credit card carries a 2.35 percent fee. Partial payments cannot be made online.
  • Drop box: outside the front lobby of Town Hall, open around the clock, no cash. A receipt is mailed the next business day.
  • Walk-in: Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Mail: send the right stub with the check, postmarked by January 10 for the first half and May 31 for the second half.

Partial payments of $200 or more plus any interest are accepted by the Receiver and by the Comptroller. A returned check adds a $20 charge.

How do I grieve a Brookhaven assessment?

File between May 1 and Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. In 2026 that was May 19, with an online application open from May 1 until the end of that day. The next one is Tuesday, May 18, 2027.

The Assessor's calendar sets March 1 as the taxable status date, the day your exemption applications are due. The tentative roll is filed May 1, and the final roll is filed July 1. Mailed grievances must be sent to the Town of Brookhaven Assessor, Attention: Grievance, at 1 Independence Hill, or left in the Assessor's bin at the main lobby security desk. In 2026 the Assessor also kept extended hours on Thursday, May 7 from 4:30 to 8 p.m. and Saturday, May 9 from 8 a.m. to noon, and the 2026 Grievance Day hearing ran from 4 to 8 p.m. on the third floor of Town Hall in the Work Session Room. Check the Grievance Day page each spring for the 2027 schedule.

Owners who file late get nothing. The town states that applications submitted before May 1 or after the Grievance Day deadline are returned to the applicant.

What happens if I sell a Brookhaven house with taxes unpaid?

Suffolk County law makes timely payment the property owner's duty even when no bill arrived, and the owner is liable for penalties and interest on late payments. Because bills go out in December, the town tells anyone who buys in Suffolk County during the following year to call the Receiver and confirm every tax is current.

  • Sellers should ask the Receiver for a current figure and note whether the first half or the whole year is paid.
  • If the bill went to a former address, give the Receiver the right mailing address.
  • After May 31, ask the Suffolk County Comptroller for the payoff. Its check address is 330 Center Drive in Riverhead.

If taxes stay unpaid until the tax lien sale, which the town says usually happens in December, the Comptroller sells a lien to Suffolk County. A cash buyer can pay off a delinquent balance at closing the same way a lender would, which avoids that sale.

What do Brookhaven housing numbers look like?

Brookhaven is mostly owner-occupied, with about four of every five homes lived in by their owners, and the average commute runs 32.3 minutes each way. Stony Brook University and Brookhaven National Laboratory together account for roughly half of the employees at the town's top ten employers, and the Long Island Rail Road serves the area.

Census QuickFacts figures for the town (2020 to 2024 survey, 2025 estimate):

  • Population estimate, July 2025: 496,410.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 80.9%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $489,200.
  • Median gross rent: $2,314.
  • Households: 166,521.

The median household income is $120,110, and the median monthly owner cost is $3,101 with a mortgage and $1,377 without one. Total area is 531.54 square miles, of which 272.11 is water, so water makes up a little over half of the town's area. If your valuation seems out of line with similar houses nearby, call the Assessor before May.

More questions about Brookhaven, NY Property Tax Guide

When are Brookhaven property taxes due?

The first half is due by January 10 and the second half by May 31. Late first-half payments add 1 percent for each month, up to 5 percent in the last three weeks of May.

Who do I pay after May 31 in Brookhaven?

The Suffolk County Comptroller, at the Suffolk County Treasurer address on Center Drive in Riverhead. A 5 percent penalty plus 1 percent a month from February 1 is added to the balance.

Can I pay Brookhaven tax by credit card?

Yes, online, with a 2.35 percent bank fee. An e-check costs $1.75. Neither fee goes to the town, and partial payments cannot be made online.

When is Brookhaven Grievance Day?

It falls on the third Tuesday in May. That was May 19 in 2026 and will be May 18 in 2027. Applications are accepted from May 1 through that day.

What if I never got a Brookhaven tax bill?

You still owe the tax and any penalties. Call the Receiver of Taxes at 631-451-9009 if the bill has not arrived by the third week of December, and keep your mailing address current.

Which offices handle property tax for a Buffalo, NY house?

Two governments bill a Buffalo house. The city department is in City Hall, Room 101, 65 Niagara Square, and answers at 716-851-5733 (option 1 reaches the Assessor) from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Erie County Real Property Tax Services is at 95 Franklin Street, Room 100, and its tax line is 716-858-8333. Buffalo sits at the head of the Niagara River on Lake Erie. It was chosen as the Erie Canal's terminus in 1825 and incorporated in 1832, and the canal made it the main inland port between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic.   • Erie County Real Property Tax Services: the county bill and its payments, online lookup and payment.

When are Buffalo property taxes due?

Ask the City of Buffalo Department of Assessment and Taxation for the current due dates on the city bill, and Erie County Real Property Tax Services for the county bill. The two bills come from different offices on different schedules.

The city's Tax Office also prepares the delinquent tax notices required under section 593 of the City Charter. If you fall behind, the department says it helps owners obtain court-ordered payment plans, and it notifies owners facing foreclosure for non-payment.

Does Buffalo reassess property every year?

Yes. Buffalo returned to annual reassessments, and owners appeal during an annual grievance window. Ask the Department of Assessment and Taxation for this year's dates, and prepare your evidence before the window opens.

You file the state complaint form RP-524 with the Department of Assessment and Taxation. A board of city residents with real estate experience reviews it. The city's budget describes plans for electronic filing and self-scheduled hearings to make the process easier. The Assessor's office reviews every sale and every deed filed in the city and also makes field inspections of old and new buildings, demolitions and fire-damaged structures, which is why a recent sale next door can move your number. The department also works with the Corporation Counsel on court cases that challenge a value and on small claims assessment review applications, so an owner who loses before the board still has a next step. Bring your own evidence to the first review: a closing statement, an appraisal, or photos of damage a field inspector could have missed.

What exemptions and relief does Buffalo list?

The city's residential exemption page lists several programs under the state's property tax law. The department processes applications and renewals for each of them.

  • School Tax Relief (STAR).
  • Senior citizen exemption for low-income owners.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited income.
  • Senior citizen longtime resident exemption.
  • Alternative veterans exemption.
  • Capital improvements exemption.

The state Tax Department now pays STAR as a credit after you register once. It issues the payment before school tax is due. The city runs an In Rem foreclosure each year and ends it with an annual auction administered by the Tax Office. Owners who fall behind receive notice before that happens, and the department can help arrange a payment plan ordered by a court.

Erie County also conducts auctions and foreclosure proceedings for unpaid county tax and publishes details through its Real Property Tax Services office. Ask the county's tax line at 716-858-8333 for a payoff figure and payment options on any account in that position. City tax, sewer rent, the county bill and any local charges get paid from your sale proceeds at the closing. Order payoff figures from both the city and Erie County, since they keep separate books.

A lower assessment in the December window feeds straight into both the city and county bills. Who bills property tax in the Town of North Hempstead?

The Town's Receiver of Taxes bills and collects school and general tax for the Town of North Hempstead, and the Nassau County Department of Assessment sets the assessments behind the bills. The town's site names Mary Jo Collins as Receiver of Taxes, and the office sits at 200 Plandome Road in Manhasset, open Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

The town covers about 54 square miles of land in Nassau County and had an estimated 238,982 residents on July 1, 2025, according to the Census Bureau. Roughly 79.5% of homes are owner-occupied, and the 2020-2024 figure for median owner-occupied value is $888,000.

What are the North Hempstead property tax due dates?

School tax and general tax run on separate calendars. The school year is July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the general tax year is January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027. If the 10th lands on a weekend or holiday, the penalty-free deadline moves to the next business day.

North Hempstead Receiver of Taxes schedule for 2026-2027 school tax and 2027 general tax
BillDueLast day without penalty
First-half schoolOctober 1, 2026November 10, 2026 (passed)
First-half generalJanuary 1, 2027February 10, 2027
Second-half schoolApril 1, 2027May 10, 2027
Second-half generalJuly 1, 2027August 10, 2027

The November 10 deadline for the first school half has already gone by as of mid-November 2026. If that bill is still open, the unpaid amount is moving toward the county's delinquent roll, so call the Receiver's office for a current figure.

How do you pay a North Hempstead tax bill?

You can pay online, by phone, by mail, or in person. The town accepts electronic checks, major credit cards, and Visa or Mastercard debit cards through its payment vendor.

  • Electronic check costs a $1.75 flat fee, a credit card costs 2.3% of the amount, and a Visa or Mastercard debit card costs a $3.95 flat fee. State law requires the payer to bear card fees.
  • Mailed payments go to the Receiver of Taxes at the Manhasset post office box printed on the bill, and the envelope must be postmarked by the due date.
  • The office has an after-hours dropbox for checks and money orders, and a kiosk handles card payments inside.
  • For the first-half 2026-27 school bill, the town also ran collection tables at parks and community centers in October.

The town warns that since December 24, 2025 a USPS postmark reflects the date a regional facility processed the mail, so a letter mailed close to a deadline can pick up a later postmark. Real Property Law section 925 does not allow a late penalty to be waived, and taxes count as paid only after the payment clears the bank.

Which school districts and villages affect a North Hempstead bill?

Your school tax goes to the district that serves your address, and your village, if you live in one, bills its own tax on top. The town's closing guide lists these district codes: Westbury, East Williston, Roslyn, Port Washington, New Hyde Park, Manhasset, Great Neck, Herricks, Mineola, Carle Place, Floral Park, Glenwood Landing and Jericho.

More than two dozen incorporated villages sit inside the town, among them Great Neck Plaza, Kings Point, Lake Success, Manorhaven, Munsey Park, Plandome, Roslyn Harbor, Russell Gardens, Saddle Rock, Sands Point, Thomaston and Williston Park. A village collects its own taxes and can use assessed values that differ from the county roll, so a seller in a village should also ask the village clerk for a balance and due date. A dispute over which district a house belongs to goes to that district or the state education commissioner, because the town has no say.

How does the school and general tax split affect a sale?

Each half-year bill covers a different slice of time, so the seller and buyer settle up based on which months each bill paid for. Per the Receiver's closing guide, the first-half school levy covers July 1 to December 31, the second-half school levy covers January 1 to June 30, the first-half general levy covers January 1 to June 30, and the second-half general levy covers July 1 to December 31.

The town's guide tells closing parties to match the closing date to these periods. A sale in November, for example, falls inside the first school half and the second general half, and a sale in April sits in the second school half and the first general half. Ask your attorney or title company for a written payoff before closing, and near a deadline ask the town for the exact penalty figure.

What happens to exemptions and restored taxes after a sale?

Exemptions generally do not move with the deed, and the buyer applies on their own with the Nassau County Department of Assessment. If an exemption ends because of a sale, Nassau County may add prorated restored taxes of up to one year to a later bill, and because of the county assessment calendar this can take up to two years to show up.

New owners must tell the Receiver of Taxes, and the incorporated village if there is one, about the new ownership, mailing address and mortgage escrow, which keeps bills from going to the wrong place. Improvements, including work done before a sale that was never reported, can raise the assessed value beyond the 6% cap.

The town also describes these programs, which the county administers:

  • STAR, which applies only to school tax. Basic STAR is open to all ages with income of $500,000 or less, and Enhanced STAR is for owners 65 and older.
  • A senior citizens exemption reducing county, town and school tax by 5% to 65% on a sliding income scale, with the top 65% tier at $47,000 of income or less.
  • Disability, veterans, and volunteer firefighter and ambulance exemptions.
  • A home improvement exemption that decreases over eight years on qualifying work.

The statewide STAR rules are covered in our New York STAR guide.

How do you challenge a North Hempstead assessment?

File an application for correction with the Nassau County Assessment Review Commission, which is separate from the Department of Assessment. The Commission says the next window follows the tentative roll set January 4, 2027, with filing open through March 1, 2027, and the town's own page lists January 2 as the opening date, so check which date the Commission shows when you file.

You can file online through AROW, in person at 240 Old Country Road in Mineola, or by asking for a paper form. There is no filing fee, and you may represent yourself or hire a representative. The Commission asks for sales of comparable homes, and its online sales locator helps you find them. If the Commission denies the appeal, a Small Claims Assessment Review petition in court is the next step. The Receiver of Taxes does not set assessments and cannot change them, and a village that keeps its own roll requires a separate filing with the Village Assessor.

What if North Hempstead property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid tax moves to the Nassau County Treasurer. For the towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead and Oyster Bay, the Treasurer's Tax Records department handles both delinquent general and school tax, starting June 1 for school tax and September 1 for general tax.

The county's page for 2026 delinquent taxes shows personal checks accepted from June 1 to November 30, 2026, credit card and electronic check payments from June 26, 2026 through January 31, 2027, and Wednesday, February 10, 2027 at 3:00 PM as the last day to pay before the lien sale. Tax liens themselves cannot be paid online and need a bank cashier's check or cash.

The state's lien and foreclosure rules are in our tax lien guide. If you plan to sell a house with unpaid tax, ask for a payoff in writing and have your closing attorney pay it from the proceeds. Your bill shows the rate for your parcel, and the Receiver's office can answer questions about it.

More questions about North Hempstead, NY Property Tax Guide

When is North Hempstead general tax due?

The first half of the 2027 general tax is due January 1, 2027, and can be paid without penalty through February 10, 2027. The second half is due July 1, 2027, with a penalty-free deadline of August 10, 2027.

Where do I pay my North Hempstead taxes in person?

At the Receiver of Taxes office, 200 Plandome Road in Manhasset, Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Bring your bill. Card payments go through the kiosk, and checks or money orders can use the after-hours dropbox.

Is the November 10, 2026 school tax deadline still open?

No. It passed on November 10, 2026, and the first-half school bill is late if still unpaid. Contact the Receiver's office about penalties, and expect delinquent amounts to be collected by the Nassau County Treasurer.

Who do I call to appeal my assessment?

The Nassau County Assessment Review Commission handles appeals, and its page lists a phone line for paper forms and questions. The Receiver of Taxes does not set or change assessments.

Do I keep my STAR benefit if I sell and move?

Not on the house you sold. The Tax Department says to close the registration when you sell, and your buyer should register for the STAR credit once the home is their primary residence.
